review.summary: A fun, weekend-buildable concept, but there is no evidence anyone wants a watch-only AI date for their OC or would pay for it, and moderation plus companion-chatbot and contest-law exposure is heavy for a near-zero-overhead owner. The only reachable audience (pro-AI OC roleplayers) is narrow and may skew young or NSFW.

items.title: Daily Date: one blind date a day to predict, no account
items.why: RESEARCH.md's strongest behavioural evidence is the Love Island habit: more than a quarter of mobile viewers played the prediction game. The launch kit dropped r/LoveIslandUSA because Botchelor has "no spectator-only hook". A single house-cast date each day at a fixed URL, predicted without an account and ending in a copyable, spoiler-free result line, gives spectators a reason to come back and so
acceptance: GET /daily returns 200 for a logged-out visitor and shows today's date number, both house characters' names and sheets, and a prediction form with exactly three choices (second_date, friends, disaster). Before a pick, the server-rendered HTML does not contain the episode's ending value or its last scene

The same UTC day always serves the same episode, a different day serves a different one, and /daily/{n} serves past day n with its ending shown. The day's episode is chosen deterministically from the house-cast pool (unit test with a frozen clock), and it works with every LLM env var unset if that day's episode is already stored

Submitting a pick without an account reveals the episode, says whether the pick was right, and keeps a streak count in localStorage: two correct days in a row show "Streak: 2" in a Playwright test that advances the clock

A "Copy result" button copies text that contains "Botchelor Daily #{n}", an emoji for right or wrong, the streak and a URL ending in /daily?ref=daily, and does not contain the ending value or either character's name
/daily has og:title containing "Botchelor Daily" and is listed in /sitemap.xml; the home page links to it above the fold; loading /daily?ref=daily sends a `visit` to the RepoHQ beacon with ref=daily

items.title: Export your OC as a SillyTavern character card
items.why: REVENUE.md's buyer is an adult who already roleplays their OC with AI, and that audience (r/SillyTavernAI, card hubs) passes characters around as V2 cards: a PNG with chara_card_v2 JSON in a tEXt chunk. Giving a creator their own Botchelor character as a card that opens in SillyTavern, with a creator_notes line pointing to its dates, adds a backlink to every card that gets shared. It also gives th
acceptance: GET /api/characters/{id}/card.png for a character owned by the requester returns 200, content-type image/png, and a tEXt chunk with keyword "chara" whose base64 JSON has spec "chara_card_v2", spec_version "2.0", and data.name, data.description (bio, want, dealbreaker) and data.personality (the three traits) equal to the character's fields (unit test parses the PNG)
data.creator_notes contains https://botchelor.com/c/{id}?ref=card and the text "AI-generated character from Botchelor (18+)", and the card contains no account name, email or private "soul" field
The same route returns 403 for a character the requester doesn't own and 404 for an unknown id; house characters and characters hidden by reports can't be exported

The character page shows a "Download SillyTavern card" button only to its owner, and a test that opens the downloaded file with @lenml/char-card-reader (or an equivalent parser) reads back the same name
GET /c/{id}?ref=card returns 200 for a logged-out visitor, shows the character's public sheet and links to its episodes and to /create, and sends a `visit` to the RepoHQ beacon with ref=card

items.title: Free blind-date / meet-cute prompt generator for two OCs
items.why: Writers already use single-purpose generators for this: Story Shack runs a dating-show concept generator, a shipping prompt generator and a meet-cute generator, and CodeItBro runs an OTP prompt generator. Botchelor's showrunner already has the setting and twist seeds these tools output. Two names in, a deterministic setting, twist and stake out, ending in "watch them actually go on this date", put
acceptance: GET /tools/meet-cute-generator returns 200 with an h1 containing "Meet-Cute Generator", two name inputs, a <title> containing "Meet-Cute" and a canonical link to itself

Submitting "Juniper" and "Dex" lands on /meet-cute/juniper/dex, which server-renders a setting, a twist and a stake drawn from the showrunner's own seed lists; the same URL gives the same scenario on reload, and "Reroll" goes to a ?v=2 variant with a different setting (deterministic, no model call, works with every LLM env var unset)
The result page links to /create with the first name prefilled and the scenario's setting passed as the date seed, and has og:title containing both names
A name on the real-person blocklist or with a sexual-content term shows the same error /create shows and renders no scenario, and the result page has noindex
/sitemap.xml lists /tools/meet-cute-generator, and the other /tools pages link to it
